answerable: Simulate daily runoff generation (surface + subsurface, QRUNOFF) at representative columns within the American River drainage.
Produce a daily basin-aggregated runoff time series that can be qualitatively compared to the shape/seasonality of the observed hydrograph.
Characterize snowmelt-driven spring freshet timing and evapotranspiration partitioning that control hydrograph shape.
not_answerable: A true routed daily STREAMFLOW hydrograph AT the USGS gauge cannot be produced by single-column ELM alone — channel routing (MOSART) plus a delineated drainage network and area weighting are required to convert column runoff (mm/s) to gauge discharge (m3/s).

A rigorous NSE against observed discharge is therefore not defensible from single-column runoff without routing; only an approximate NSE on area-scaled, un-routed runoff can be reported and it will be biased low on timing/attenuation.

parsed.n_justification: The American River basin above the Nile gauge spans ~350-1977 m elevation; runoff is dominated by an elevation-banded snowpack. Three columns representing low (rain/rain-snow), mid (transitional snow), and high (seasonal snowpack) elevation bands capture the dominant control on freshet timing and volume while keeping the design tractable for a site archetype.
requires_capabilities: MOSART channel routing coupled to ELM to convert gridded/column runoff to discharge at the gauge outlet
Sub-basin delineation and drainage-area weighting for the American River above USGS Nile gauge to aggregate the three elevation-band columns
USGS daily discharge retrieval and NSE computation utility (obs-vs-sim alignment, unit conversion mm/s -> m3/s)
Elevation-band area fractions (hypsometry) to weight columns
assumptions: Gauge is USGS 'American River near Nile, WA' at approximately 46.98N, -121.17W; exact column coordinates place elevation bands within the contributing area.

Single-column runoff is treated as instantaneous local generation; without MOSART no in-channel travel time, storage, or attenuation is represented, so simulated peaks will be early/flashier than observed.
Forcing is the standard GSWP3/CLMNCEP-style dataset available 1980-2018; a spin-up (recycled early years) is assumed prior to the analysis period.
Column soil textures are approximate glacial/volcanic mountain profiles; a surface dataset with local soil/PFT is assumed available.

Reported NSE, if required now, will be computed on area-weighted un-routed daily runoff versus observed discharge and clearly flagged as an upper-bound-timing-limited approximation; a defensible NSE requires the routing capability above.
